title: Core rows sync to QuickBooks under the core part's category item
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner/Admin user (that role holds every permission, including Part sales - Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments - Create & Edit).
  • A test customer exists.
  • QuickBooks Online is connected to this shop (the QuickBooks test company).
  • The core's part category (the category the part uses, "Uncategorized" if none was chosen) is mapped to a QuickBooks item (for example "Parts").
  • A test vendor exists to order parts from.
  • The first sale: a new part sale started today for the test customer (a sale started before this release handles cores the old way), with the part "Water Pump" (Quantity 1; Vendor = the test vendor; Sell Price $517.55; Core Charge $79.99) and, beneath it, a row "Core for Water Pump".
  • On the first sale the part is authorized, ordered and received, and the core has been returned: the core row's Status reads Returned, and the document on the Finance tab has a Core credit row of -$79.99.
  • The second sale (for the unmapped check): built exactly like the first, but with the part's Category set to "ZZAUTOTEST No QuickBooks item", a category whose QuickBooks Products And Services is empty; it is ordered, received and its core returned too.
custom_steps:
1. On the first sale's Finance tab click Create Invoice and let it sync to QuickBooks.
  2. Open the resulting invoice in QuickBooks and find the core charge line and the Core credit line.
  3. Read each line's item, amount and tax, and confirm the Core credit is a negative invoice line (not a credit memo).
  4. Add the two core amounts on that item together.
  5. Create Invoice on the second sale (unmapped item), then open the Unexported report.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The core charge line ($79.99) and the Core credit line (-$79.99) both sit on the QuickBooks item mapped to the core's part category, so the returned core nets to $0.00 on that one item ($79.99 + -$79.99 = $0.00).
  • The Core credit is a negative invoice line of -$79.99 with the same parts tax treatment - not a QuickBooks credit memo.
  • For the second sale, the whole invoice is held back and listed in the Unexported report until the item is mapped; no line is dropped and none is sent under a different item.
  • Any fee or discount rows post on the shop's fee and discount items, as on a work order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 5 Oct 2026 (specification edited that day). Source-verified 5 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R17: “The core charge row and its Core credit row both take the QuickBooks item from the product and service mapped to the core's part category, so a returned core nets to $0 on that one item”
  • S1-R17: “The Core credit row is a negative line, -$79.99 on a $79.99 core, with the same parts tax treatment; it is a negative line on the invoice, not a QuickBooks credit memo, so it reduces the revenue the core charge row adds”
  • S1-R17: “If a line's product and service has no QuickBooks item, the whole invoice is held back and lands in the Unexported report until it is mapped, exactly as a work order invoice with an unmapped part line. No row is ever dropped and none is sent under a substitute item”
  • S1-R17: “Fee and discount rows post on the shop's fee and discount items, as on a work order”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
